chunks: And it is narrated from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Sayābah, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Indeed, ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr instructed me to ask you. He said: We borrow bread from the neighbors, then we return bread smaller than it or larger.
So he عليه السلام said: We borrow walnuts, sixty and seventy by number, and among them there may be small and large ones, so there is no harm in that.

key_terms.أَصْغَرَ: smaller in size than the original
key_terms.أَكْبَرَ: larger in size than the original
key_terms.عَدَدًا: by numerical count rather than exact measured equality
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.ٱلْجَوْزَ: walnuts used as the Imam’s example
key_terms.ٱلْجِيرَانِ: neighbors from whom the item is borrowed
key_terms.ٱلْخُبْزَ: bread as the borrowed item in question

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to return borrowed bread or counted items in a slightly smaller or larger size?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates the permissibility of returning borrowed fungible goods with minor variation in size when the exchange is by customary equivalence and not intended as usury. The Imam عليه السلام illustrates this through the example of borrowing walnuts by count, where natural variation between small and large items does not create a problem.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3707 - It is narrated from Al-Sabbah ibn Sayabah who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (as), "Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur instructed me to ask you-when we borrow bread from our neighbors, we sometimes return it smaller or larger in size. Is this permissible?"
Imam (as) said: "We borrow walnuts, sixty or seventy in number, and they may include small and large ones. There is no harm in this."
